context.analysis:
## Overview
- Real-time payment fraud screening system for card-not-present transactions on AWS.
- Screens authorizations in under 50ms, manages analyst reviews, and ensures strict PCI-DSS compliance.

## Key Elements
- Merchant / Payment Gateway (Upstream client system)
- Fraud Analyst (Internal user managing reviews and rules)
- Fraud Screening Engine (Core AWS Fargate containerized system)
- API Gateway (Edge router with perimeter tokenization)
- AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock (Tamper-evident audit archive)
- Card Schemes / External Enrichment APIs (External risk data sources)

## Relationships
- Merchant to API Gateway: Sends payment authorizations via HTTPS/JSON over TLS 1.3 / mTLS.
- Fraud Analyst to Fraud Screening Engine: Accesses case management via HTTPS with RBAC and MFA.
- API Gateway to Fraud Screening Engine: Internal communication using gRPC.
- Fraud Screening Engine to AWS QLDB/S3: Asynchronously writes audit logs and decision metadata.
- Fraud Screening Engine to External Enrichment APIs: Fetches auxiliary risk signals via HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- AWS Fargate: Container execution platform minimizing management overhead for a three-engineer team.
- AWS API Gateway & Route 53: Perimeter routing enforcing tokenization, TLS 1.3, and fail-open controls.
- gRPC: Internal communication protocol ensuring P99 decision latency remains below 50 ms.
- AWS QLDB & S3 Object Lock: WORM-compliant storage guaranteeing tamper-evident 7-year auditability.
- Terraform: Infrastructure-as-Code enforcing strict budget limits under 25,000 EUR per month.

## Rationale
- The single-region AWS Fargate architecture respects the operational capacity of a three-engineer team and the 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint. Perimeter tokenization and gRPC internals fulfill PCI-DSS Level 1 security requirements and sub-50ms latency targets.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations to protect transactions before approval while supporting suspicious payment reviews. It processes high-throughput financial transactions securely within strict latency, compliance, and budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- **People**: Merchant / Payment Gateway, Fraud Analyst, Merchant Risk Manager, Compliance Auditor
- **Systems**: Card Schemes / External Enrichment APIs, AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock
- **Containers**: API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy (Envoy/AWS API Gateway), Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go / AWS ECS on Fargate), Case Management API (Node.js/Java Spring Boot), Audit Log Sitter (Rust), Rule & Model Distribution Service (Python/FastAPI + S3), Event Broker (AWS MSK / Managed Kafka or AWS SQS)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway to API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- API Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Engine via gRPC over AWS VPC private subnets with native TLS
- Real-Time Scoring Engine to Event Broker via TCP/TLS
- Event Broker to Audit Log Sitter and Case Management API via TCP/TLS
- Fraud Analyst and Compliance Auditor to Case Management API via HTTPS (OAuth2/OIDC, MFA)

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: AWS ECS on Fargate with Fargate Spot for cost optimization (fits 25,000 EUR/month budget and 3-person team).
- **Languages**: Go (scoring engine performance), Rust (audit logging), Python/FastAPI (model distribution), Node.js/Java (case management).
- **Security & Networking**: TLS 1.3, AWS VPC Lattice / native TLS, AWS KMS (CMK), AWS Secrets Manager, AWS Private CA.
- **Data & Messaging**: Redis (model caching), AWS MSK or AWS SQS (decoupling), AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock (tamper-evident audit storage).

## Rationale
The containerized microservices architecture cleanly separates high-performance, stateless real-time scoring from audit and case management, ensuring P99 latency remains below 50 ms at 3,000 TPS. Utilizing managed AWS serverless and container services minimizes operational overhead for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening engine deployed on AWS eu-west-1, designed to score card-not-present payment authorizations and manage fraud reviews.]
[Its core purpose is to deliver sub-50ms fraud decisions while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a strict budget.]

## Key Elements
- API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy (Envoy Proxy on AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Edge Router Component (Envoy)
- Tokenization Filter Component (Native Envoy C++/Lua configuration with Format-Preserving Encryption)
- Payload Sanitizer Component
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go on AWS ECS on Fargate with Redis)
- Case Management API (Node.js / Java Spring Boot)
- Audit Log Sitter (Rust)
- Rule & Model Distribution Service (Python / FastAPI + S3)
- Event Broker (AWS MSK / Managed Kafka or AWS SQS)
- AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> AWS Network Load Balancer: Sends payment authorizations [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- AWS Network Load Balancer -> API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy: Forwards traffic [TCP]
- API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Routes requests for scoring [gRPC over AWS VPC private subnets with mTLS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Event Broker: Publishes scoring results and telemetry [Kafka/SQS]
- Audit Log Sitter -> AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Writes tamper-evident logs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS eu-west-1: Target cloud region for compliance and infrastructure constraints.
- Envoy Proxy / AWS ECS on Fargate: Powers the edge gateway with auto-scaling to handle 3,000 TPS under a 3-engineer team.
- Format-Preserving Encryption (FPE): Enables low-latency stateless PAN tokenization without expensive HSM round-trips.
- gRPC with mTLS: Ensures secure, high-performance internal service-to-service communication.
- AWS X-Ray and JSON structured logging: Provides distributed tracing and observability.

## Rationale
[This architecture achieves P99 latency under 50ms at 3,000 TPS through localized tokenization, native Envoy filters, and stateless Fargate auto-scaling. It satisfies strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, auditability, and a 1-minute fail-open availability requirement within the €25,000 monthly budget and 3-engineer operational limits.]

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud within strict latency constraints, providing case management tools for fraud analysts. It operates on AWS to meet PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining a fixed infrastructure budget.]

## Key Elements
- [API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy (Envoy / AWS API Gateway)]
- [Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go / AWS ECS on Fargate, Redis)]
- [Rule & Model Distribution Service (Python / FastAPI + S3)]
- [Event Broker (AWS MSK / Managed Kafka)]
- [Fraud Analyst]

## Relationships
- [API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Routes requests for scoring using gRPC over AWS VPC private subnets with mTLS]
- [Real-Time Scoring Engine <-> Redis Cluster: Fetches sliding-window velocity counters using Redis RESP protocol over TLS]
- [Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Event Broker (AWS MSK): Publishes cryptographically signed scoring events using Kafka protocol over TLS with SASL/IAM]
- [Rule & Model Distribution Service -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Delivers rules and models via S3 with cryptographic verification]

## Technology Stack
- [Go: Powers the Real-Time Scoring Engine for ultra-low latency and zero-allocation parsing]
- [AWS ECS on Fargate: Runs containerized services with auto-scaling to satisfy performance and budget constraints]
- [Redis Cluster: Provides high-throughput, in-memory state management for velocity checks]
- [AWS MSK (Managed Kafka): Handles asynchronous event streaming for audit logs and telemetry]
- [AWS S3 & KMS: Stores encrypted models and rules with cryptographic signature verification]

## Rationale
[This architecture utilizes Go on AWS Fargate with Redis to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within a strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Security and auditability requirements (PCI-DSS Level 1, cryptographic signing) are met through mTLS, IAM policies, and tamper-evident event logging.]

Case Management API.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that processes card-not-present payment authorizations and provides case management for fraud analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining a low-latency, highly available architecture within a fixed infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst / Compliance Auditor (Users)
- API Gateway / Tokenization Proxy (Envoy / AWS API Gateway)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go / AWS ECS on Fargate, Redis)
- Case Management API (Java Spring Boot 3.x, AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Event Broker (AWS MSK / Managed Kafka)
- Audit Log Sitter (Rust)
- Persistence & Storage (AWS RDS PostgreSQL with AWS KMS, AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management API: Accesses case management workflows, bulk actions, and metrics via HTTPS (OAuth2/OIDC, MFA) [TLS 1.3]
- Compliance Auditor -> Case Management API: Accesses audit and compliance records via HTTPS (OAuth2/OIDC, MFA) [TLS 1.3]
- Event Broker -> Case Management API: Streams review events and case data via TCP/TLS [mTLS]
- Case Management API -> AWS RDS PostgreSQL: Persists case states, SLA tracking, and audit data via JDBC [TLS 1.3]
- Case Management API -> Audit Log Sitter: Sends cryptographically signed action records via TCP/TLS [mTLS]

## Technology Stack
- Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.x: Core framework for the Case Management API, providing enterprise security ecosystems.
- Spring Batch: Handles parallelized batch state transitions for bulk case operations.
- AWS RDS PostgreSQL: Encrypted relational database for case state management, secured with AWS KMS CMK.
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Container orchestration enforcing strict CPU and memory ceilings for the 3-engineer team.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Manages and rotates database credentials and OIDC client secrets every 30 days.

## Rationale
This architecture uses enterprise-grade Java frameworks and AWS managed services to guarantee strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, tamper-evident 7-year auditability, and high availability. It balances robust security controls, automated scaling, and operational simplicity to fit a three-engineer team and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Audit Log Sitter.analysis:
## Overview
The Audit Log Sitter collects and securely routes real-time payment audit events to tamper-evident immutable storage. It ensures strict regulatory compliance and zero data loss for downstream consumers like compliance officers and external auditors.

## Key Elements
- Audit Log Sitter (Rust / AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Kafka Consumer Component (`rdkafka`)
- Payload Normalizer & Signer Component
- WORM Storage Batcher Component
- Resilience & DLQ Router Component
- AWS MSK (Managed Kafka)
- AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock
- AWS KMS
- Terraform

## Relationships
- AWS MSK -> Audit Log Sitter: Streams audit payloads [TCP/TLS 1.3 with mTLS]
- Kafka Consumer Component -> Resilience & DLQ Router Component: Passes failed/poisoned payloads [In-memory channel]
- Payload Normalizer & Signer Component -> WORM Storage Batcher Component: Passes normalized signed payloads [In-memory channel]
- WORM Storage Batcher Component -> AWS S3 Object Lock / QLDB: Persists audit logs [HTTPS / TLS 1.3 with IAM Condition Keys and `aws:SecureTransport`]

## Technology Stack
- Rust: Chosen for low memory footprint, performance, and safety suitable for a 3-person team
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Minimizes operational overhead and auto-scales based on consumer lag
- AWS S3 Object Lock & QLDB: Provides 7-year WORM storage in Compliance Mode for auditability (R-06)
- AWS MSK with Dead-Letter Queues: Handles event streaming and isolates poisoned payloads
- AWS KMS: Manages cryptographic keys securely for payload signing and PCI-DSS compliance

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to remain within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget while requiring only three engineers to operate. It enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail through TLS 1.3, mTLS, AWS KMS, and S3 Object Lock Compliance Mode.

Event Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Event Broker provides real-time, fault-tolerant message streaming for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It decouples high-throughput card-not-present payment authorizations while ensuring strict auditability and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Topic Router & Partition Manager**: Manages topic creation, partition assignment, and high-throughput routing using hashed card ID keys.
- **Access Control & Auth Enforcer**: Validates mutual TLS (mTLS) certificates and enforces Kafka ACLs to isolate the `audit-log` topic.
- **Storage & Replication Engine**: Handles 3-AZ log replication and encrypted-at-rest persistence via AWS KMS CMKs.
- **Producers & Consumers**: Real-Time Scoring Engine, Audit Log Sitter, and Case Management API.
- **Infrastructure Services**: AWS Secrets Manager, S3 Object Lock, and AWS CloudWatch.

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Topic Router: Publishes authorization events and telemetry [TCP/TLS 1.3, Kafka Protocol]
- Topic Router -> Audit Log Sitter: Streams audit events via dedicated consumer group [TCP/TLS 1.3, Kafka Protocol]
- Topic Router -> Case Management API: Streams events for case creation [TCP/TLS 1.3, Kafka Protocol]
- Access Control & Auth Enforcer -> AWS Secrets Manager: Validates mTLS certificates and credentials [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Storage Engine -> S3 Object Lock Bucket: Offloads tamper-evident audit streams asynchronously [AWS PrivateLink]

## Technology Stack
- **AWS MSK (Managed Kafka)**: Provisioned `kafka.m5.large` instances across 3 Availability Zones to guarantee high availability and stable cost control under 25,000 EUR/month.
- **TLS 1.3 & mTLS**: Secures all data-in-transit and authenticates internal services.
- **AWS KMS**: Provides customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest.
- **Terraform / GitHub Actions**: Automates infrastructure provisioning and zero-downtime deployments.

## Rationale
Provisioned AWS MSK with 3-AZ deployment reliably sustains 3,000 TPS under the 50 ms latency threshold while maintaining a strict budget for a 3-engineer team. Strict topic isolation and S3 Object Lock meet 7-year tamper-evident auditability and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance mandates.
